title: Crypto Utilities
description: Hashing, encryption, and HMAC in JavaScript.

data.text: Crypto-js provides standard cryptographic algorithms for hashing, encryption, and encoding in JavaScript.

data.title: SHA-256 hash with crypto-js

data.text: crypto-js implements common algorithms in JavaScript: SHA-256 for digests, HMAC for message authentication, AES for symmetric encryption, and base64/hex encoding. The Web Crypto API in the browser covers most of these natively and is the better default.

data.title: A hash and an HMAC

data.text: Encryption Needs a Real Key and IV

AES in CBC mode requires a random initialization vector that is stored alongside the ciphertext; reusing a fixed IV with the same key leaks information. A password must never be used directly as a key — derive one with PBKDF2 and a per-user salt.

data.title: Encrypt with a random IV and PBKDF2-derived key
Do not hand-roll cryptography in the browser
data.text: Client-side JavaScript crypto cannot protect a secret from the user running the page, and rolling your own construction invites mistakes such as a reused IV or a weak password-to-key derivation. Use Web Crypto, use well-reviewed libraries, and do anything security-critical — password hashing, token signing — on the server. Treat this lesson as understanding, not as a recipe.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never rely solely on client-side security.
